task.title: Add optimistic web mutation queue
task.description:
Make web mutations render immediately while HTTP success remains Git-durable. Send the client-observed task head, queue pending intents sequentially per task, persist independent tasks concurrently, reconcile confirmed responses, roll back failed intents without clobbering later actions, surface stale-head conflicts, and cover projection and request races.

Also bring the board onto the auto-sync workflow from WB-01KYT0RX395F6VG7RYZSZTF1A3, which deliberately left `serve` local-only. Show the current auto-sync state in the UI and let the user toggle it to shift modes.

The synchronization half of that is now cheaper than this task assumed. WB-01KZ1HX00S59FMEBX1JWJK7KS7 added a sync loop that `serve` already hosts, so the board observes other clones' work without any change here; what remains is making web mutations publish. Do that by nudging the loop after a mutation rather than by applying fetch-before/push-after inline in the HTTP handler. Inline would cost every web mutation two network round trips, roughly 530 ms and 16 Git processes measured on the CLI path, which is exactly the latency the optimistic queue exists to hide. A nudge is a receipt-only exchange, so the handler returns as soon as the write is durable and publication follows behind it.

Reuse the CLI's deferral path rather than inventing a second one. It probes for a watcher, writes locally, nudges, and falls back to an inline push when no watcher answers, and it works unchanged whether the loop is the one `serve` started or an external `workbook sync --watch` that owns the socket first. That fallback matters here: `serve` runs no loop of its own when an external watcher already owns the repository, so a handler must not assume the in-process loop exists.

One piece is missing rather than free. `syncloop.Run` is fire-and-forget and exposes no in-process nudge, so either it grows a handle for its host, or the handler dials the published socket the way the CLI does. Dialing is the smaller change and keeps one code path for both cases.

Given this, the auto-sync UI toggle is now about whether to defer or to synchronize inline, not about whether the board synchronizes at all.
